the_argument_summary: The axial-symmetry critique of the dome model is best stated as a NAMED INVARIANT that is version-independent, dimensionality-argued, and quotable: 'No radial-only field model can encode longitude-dependent structure — refining the radial profile cannot rescue it.' Any function H(r) — no matter how sophisticated the r-dependence (exponential, power-law, piecewise, spline-fitted) — depends on ONE spatial variable and thus generates a 1-D scalar field over the disc. The observations the dome claims to predict (SAA two-cell structure, NMP longitudinal trajectory, hemispheric asymmetry) require a 2-D scalar field (r, theta) over the disc — irreducibly, because they DEPEND ON longitude. This is a dimensionality mismatch, not a fitting problem, and no refinement in the radial-only class can close it. Formally: the space of functions f(r) is a proper subspace of the space of functions f(r, theta), and the observed longitude-dependent structure lives outside the subspace. Naming this as an invariant means every dome version bump that ships a new H(r) — V51.2, V52, and every future variant — is answered by pointing at the same named principle rather than reinventing the argument for each new radial profile. The invariant is quotable, testable ('is the new equation radial-only?'), and cross-page linkable (the model tab, self-contradictions, kill shots, and predictions can all cite the same named object).
kernel_of_truth: The axial-symmetry critique in Section 2.10 is already strong — it shows the SAA has two lobes at specific longitudes (Atlantic near 50W, African near 20E), that the dome's B(r) equation with two exponential sources still cannot produce two independently drifting local minima, and that the observed field morphology requires spherical harmonic degree 2 minimum (8 coefficients) vs the dome's 4 parameters, with IGRF-13 using degree 13 (195 coefficients). This is empirically decisive. The named-invariant framing does not add new evidence — it packages the existing evidence into a version-independent principle. That is exactly the right move given the dome's 13-version release history: every V-bump has refined the radial profile, and every future refinement will do the same. Naming the invariant is what makes the critique durable across future dome versions.
arithmetic_derivation_notes: The mathematical statement: let F_r be the space of scalar functions on the disc that depend only on radial distance r from the pole. Let F_rt be the space of scalar functions on the disc that may depend on both r and longitude theta. Then F_r is a proper subspace of F_rt — a function in F_r evaluates to the same value at (r, 0) and (r, pi), so it cannot represent any observable whose value differs at those two points. The SAA has observationally-distinct field values at 50W and 20E at the same magnetic-latitude ring; therefore any function that reproduces the SAA is in F_rt minus F_r, and no element of F_r can be a legitimate representation of the observed field. This is a subspace-inclusion argument, not a fitting-quality argument, and it is stable under any parametric refinement within F_r. Any new dome H(r) — however sophisticated — is still in F_r, so still cannot reach the observation. The invariant thus applies to all past and future dome versions of the H(r) family.

anticipated_objections.objection: The dome can add a theta-dependent correction later — the invariant will just get updated to describe whichever new class the dome uses.
anticipated_objections.response: Correct — and if the dome adds explicit longitude dependence, our critique adapts: the new equation is no longer radial-only and the invariant no longer applies to that particular version. What the invariant PREVENTS is a series of radial-only refinements (V51.2, V52, V53...) each claimed to fix the axial-symmetry problem. A radial-only refinement cannot fix a dimensionality mismatch by construction — a fact stated as an invariant, not rediscovered each version. If the dome ships a genuinely non-radial equation, that is a substantive step and we credit it; the invariant survives as the principle that forced that step.

Naming a principle is what turns evidence into a durable, version-independent argument.

anticipated_objections.objection: Naming the invariant is just relabeling.
anticipated_objections.response: Relabeling is what turns a scattered set of empirical observations into a rebuttable principle. Compare: 'the SAA has two lobes at specific longitudes and the dome cannot produce them' (an empirical claim, potentially rebuttable case-by-case) vs 'no radial-only model can encode longitude-dependent structure' (an invariant, rebuttable only by exiting the radial-only class). The second framing forces the dome author into a categorical choice — abandon radial-only or abandon the longitude-dependent WINs — rather than a narrative about whether some new H(r) fits better.

The existing empirical evidence (12 WINs listed, spherical-harmonic degree comparison, dual-lobe test, mathematical impossibility of two independently drifting minima from a two-exponential sum) then reads as the demonstration of the invariant rather than the argument for a conclusion. The invariant is short enough to be linkable from other tabs — model tab, kill-shots tab, predictions tab can all use a single hyperlink to the named block.

prose_patches.old: The observed SAA directly falsifies this. Since at least 1850, the anomaly has consisted of two distinct lobes: an Atlantic lobe (centered near 50°W) and an African lobe (centered near 20°E). These lobes are not mirror images — they drift at different rates (the African lobe moves eastward while the Atlantic lobe moves westward) and decay at different speeds (WIN-005 correctly notes the African cell's faster decay). Their angular separation has grown from ~31° to ~51° over 2000–2025 (CHAOS-7 data, which the dome itself cites for WIN-004). Reproducing two independently drifting local minima requires at minimum quadrupolar structure — spherical harmonic degree 2, which needs 8 Gauss coefficients. The SAA's full morphology, including the lobe shapes, drift rates, and depth asymmetry, requires degree 4 or higher (24+ coefficients). IGRF-13 uses degree 13: 195 coefficients encoding the complete 3D field structure. The dome's 4 parameters cannot even reach degree 2.

Version durability of the invariant

The radial-only impossibility invariant stated at the top of this section is durable across dome version bumps in a way that empirical counterexamples are not. The dome has shipped 13 named versions between the original V-1 disc model and V51.1, and each version has typically refined the radial profile — different exponential decay constants, additional damping terms, source-count adjustments in B(r), tweaks to the sun and moon altitudes that feed into the field derivation. Every one of those refinements has remained inside the radial-only class of functions f(r), and every one of those refinements has therefore inherited the same dimensionality gap against longitude-dependent observations. When V51.2 or V52 or V53 ships, the response is not to redo the SAA / NMP / hemispheric-asymmetry evidence for each — the response is to point at the invariant and confirm the new equation is still radial-only. The only way to answer the critique is to exit the radial-only class by publishing an explicitly θ-dependent field equation, which the dome has not done as of V51.1 and which would itself be a substantive methodological step we would credit.
